title: Two-dimensional Wick limits and a constructive interaction interface

items.title: Cross-covariance of finite Gaussian Wick powers

references.title: Barry Simon, The P(φ)₂ Euclidean (Quantum) Field Theory, Chapter I, §1.1 (publisher preview)
references.locator: PDF pp. 24–33, printed pp. 4–13: Gaussian random variables, the Wick generating function, and Theorem 1.3 on the covariance of two Wick powers. The coefficient argument is reproduced locally for the stated finite Gaussian interface.

references.title: Stephen J. Summers, A Perspective on Constructive Quantum Field Theory, §3.1
references.locator: PDF pp. 10–12: Wick ordering for the Euclidean free field and its role in P(φ)₂; the finite Gaussian identity is proved locally here.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(X,Y)$ have a centered, possibly degenerate, jointly Gaussian law with covariance matrix $\begin{pmatrix}\sigma^2&c\\c&\tau^2\end{pmatrix}$, where $\sigma^2,\tau^2\ge0$ and the matrix is positive semidefinite. Define $:X^n:_{\sigma^2}$ and $:Y^m:_{\tau^2}$ by the finite covariance Wick-power generating identity. For all integers $n,m\ge0$,

$$\mathbb E\bigl[:X^n:_{\sigma^2}:Y^m:_{\tau^2}\bigr]=\begin{cases}n!c^n,&n=m,\\0,&n\ne m,\end{cases}$$

with $c^0:=1$.

items.title: Mollified massive two-dimensional Gaussian Wick powers

references.title: Barry Simon, The P(φ)₂ Euclidean (Quantum) Field Theory, Chapter I, §1.1 (publisher preview)
references.locator: PDF pp. 24–33, printed pp. 4–13: Gaussian random variables, measure-dependent Wick powers, and their formal generating function. The continuum covariance and mollifier conventions are stated explicitly here.

references.title: Stephen J. Summers, A Perspective on Constructive Quantum Field Theory, §3 opening and §3.1
references.locator: PDF pp. 9–12: the centered massive two-dimensional Euclidean Gaussian field, covariance (−Δ+m²)⁻¹, and Wick ordering of the free field.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, its countable-family consequence, and $m>0$. Let $\Phi$ be the real centered Gaussian random tempered distribution on $\mathbb R^2$ with covariance $C_m(f,g)=(2\pi)^{-2}\int_{\mathbb R^2}\overline{\widehat f(p)}\widehat g(p)(|p|^2+m^2)^{-1}\,d^2p$ for real Schwartz tests and $\widehat f(p)=\int e^{-ip\cdot x}f(x)\,d^2x$. Fix one nonnegative $\rho\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$ with $\int\rho(x)\,d^2x=1$, set $\rho_\epsilon(x)=\epsilon^{-2}\rho(x/\epsilon)$ for $\epsilon>0$, and define $\Phi_\epsilon(x)=\Phi(u\mapsto\rho_\epsilon(x-u))$. For each $n\ge0$, define the finite-cutoff Wick polynomial $:\!\Phi_\epsilon(x)^n\!:$ by

$$\exp\!\left(t\Phi_\epsilon(x)-\tfrac12t^2\mathbb E[\Phi_\epsilon(x)^2]\right)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}:\!\Phi_\epsilon(x)^n\!:\,\frac{t^n}{n!}$$

as an identity of formal power series. For a bounded measurable $f:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb C$ that vanishes outside a bounded set, define its cutoff smearing by the samplewise Lebesgue integral $W_{\epsilon,n}(f)=\int f(x):\!\Phi_\epsilon(x)^n\!:\,d^2x$. Every tempered sample gives a smooth $x\mapsto\Phi_\epsilon(x)$, so this integral is finite for each sample; its $L^2(\mu_C)$ limit as $\epsilon\downarrow0$ is a separate theorem, not part of this definition.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, its countable-family consequence, $m>0$, and the fixed mollifier from the earlier cutoff definition. Let $C_m$ be the translation-invariant covariance distribution whose Fourier multiplier is $(|p|^2+m^2)^{-1}$ in the convention $\widehat f(p)=\int e^{-ip\cdot x}f(x)\,d^2x$. It is represented by the even locally integrable function

$$G_m(z)=\frac1{4\pi}\int_0^\infty t^{-1}\exp\!\left(-m^2t-\frac{|z|^2}{4t}\right)dt,\qquad z\ne0.$$

There are constants $K_m,K_{m,R}<\infty$ such that $|G_m(z)|\le K_m(1+|\log|z||)$ for $0<|z|\le1$, $|G_m(z)|\le K_m e^{-m|z|}/\sqrt{m|z|}$ for $|z|\ge1$, and $G_m^q\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^2)$ for every finite $q\ge1$. For the mollified fields of the earlier cutoff definition, $\kappa_{\epsilon,\delta}(w)=\int\rho_\epsilon(a)\rho_\delta(a-w)\,d^2a$ and $C_{\epsilon,\delta}=G_m*\kappa_{\epsilon,\delta}$ satisfy $\mathbb E[\Phi_\epsilon(x)\Phi_\delta(y)]=C_{\epsilon,\delta}(x-y)$. Moreover, $C_{\epsilon,\delta}(z)\to G_m(z)$ for every $z\ne0$ as $\epsilon,\delta\downarrow0$, and for every $R>0$ there are $K_{m,R},\epsilon_{m,R}>0$ with

$$|C_{\epsilon,\delta}(z)|\le K_{m,R}(1+|\log|z||)\quad(0<|z|\le R,\ 0<\epsilon,\delta\le\epsilon_{m,R}).$$

items.title: Smeared Wick powers have a two-dimensional L² limit

references.title: Stephen J. Summers, A Perspective on Constructive Quantum Field Theory, §3 opening and §3.1
references.locator: PDF pp. 9–12: the massive two-dimensional Euclidean Gaussian covariance and Wick ordering in P(φ)₂. The local L² convergence proof is supplied here.

references.title: Barry Simon, The P(φ)₂ Euclidean (Quantum) Field Theory, Chapter I, §1.1 (publisher preview)
references.locator: PDF pp. 24–33, printed pp. 4–13: Theorem 1.3 computes the covariance of two finite Gaussian Wick powers by expanding their generating functions. The smoothing and two-dimensional kernel estimates are proved locally here.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, its countable-family consequence, and $m>0$. Let $\Phi$, $\mu_C$, the fixed nonnegative mollifier $\rho$, $\Phi_\epsilon$, and $W_{\epsilon,n}(f)$ be as in the earlier cutoff definition. Here $L^2(\mu_C)$ is the space of square-integrable complex random variables modulo almost-everywhere equality, with norm $\|X\|_2=(\mathbb E_{\mu_C}|X|^2)^{1/2}$. For every integer $n\ge1$ and every bounded measurable compactly supported $f:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb C$, the family $W_{\epsilon,n}(f)$ is Cauchy in $L^2(\mu_C)$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$; write its limit as $W_n(f)$. If $f$ is real-valued, then $W_n(f)$ is a real $L^2$-class. For all such $f,g$,

$$\mathbb E_{\mu_C}[\overline{W_n(f)}W_n(g)]=n!\int_{\mathbb R^2}\int_{\mathbb R^2}\overline{f(x)}g(y)G_m(x-y)^n\,d^2x\,d^2y.$$

The kernel satisfies $|G_m(z)|\le K_m(1+|\log|z||)$ for $0<|z|\le1$ and $|G_m(z)|\le K_m e^{-m|z|}/\sqrt{m|z|}$ for $|z|\ge1$, as established by the earlier covariance-kernel analysis.

items.title: Stable $P(φ)_2$ construction contract

references.title: Stephen J. Summers, A Perspective on Constructive Quantum Field Theory, §3.1
references.locator: PDF pp. 10–12: finite-volume P(φ)₂ tilts, the need for exponential integrability, and the distinct small-coupling qualifications of cluster-expansion results. This item specifies a contract and does not import those proofs.

references.title: Barry Simon, The P(φ)₂ Euclidean (Quantum) Field Theory, Chapter I, §1.1 (publisher preview)
references.locator: PDF pp. 24–33, printed pp. 4–13: Gaussian fields and measure-dependent Wick powers. The stronger interaction construction obligations are stated explicitly here.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and its countable-family consequence, fix $m>0$, and let $P(s)=\sum_{j=0}^{2k}a_js^j$ be a real polynomial of even degree $2k\ge2$ with $a_{2k}>0$. Let $\Phi_\epsilon$, $W_{\epsilon,j}$, and their real $L^2(\mu_C)$ limits $W_j$ for real smearings be as in the earlier cutoff definition and Wick-limit theorem. Here $\epsilon$ is the smoothing cutoff, and $\Lambda$ is a bounded Lebesgue-measurable set with finite Lebesgue area $|\Lambda|$. An exhaustion $\Lambda\nearrow\mathbb R^2$ means a directed family of such sets whose union is $\mathbb R^2$ and such that every compact subset of $\mathbb R^2$ is contained in some member. Define $U_{\Lambda,\epsilon}=a_0|\Lambda|+\sum_{j=1}^{2k}a_jW_{\epsilon,j}(\mathbf1_\Lambda)$ and $U_\Lambda=a_0|\Lambda|+\sum_{j=1}^{2k}a_jW_j(\mathbf1_\Lambda)$; $\mathbf1_\Lambda$ is bounded and compactly supported, so the Wick-limit theorem applies. For coupling $\lambda\ge0$, put $X_{\Lambda,\epsilon}=\exp(-\lambda U_{\Lambda,\epsilon})$, $X_\Lambda=\exp(-\lambda U_\Lambda)$ and define the extended nonnegative normalization $Z_\Lambda=\mathbb E_{\mu_C}X_\Lambda\in[0,+\infty]$. Only if $0<Z_\Lambda<\infty$ does the formula $d\mu_{\Lambda,\lambda}=Z_\Lambda^{-1}X_\Lambda\,d\mu_C$ define a normalized probability measure.

A construction contract for a specified polynomial, mass, coupling regime, region class, and ultraviolet/infinite-volume cutoff family is complete only after a proof establishes all of the following: (i) each $X_{\Lambda,\epsilon}$ is integrable and the family is uniformly integrable, meaning $\lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_{0<\epsilon\le1}\mathbb E_{\mu_C}[X_{\Lambda,\epsilon}\mathbf1_{\{X_{\Lambda,\epsilon}>R\}}]=0$; (ii) the cutoff normalizations converge to a strictly positive finite $Z_\Lambda$ and, for every stated polynomial/test insertion $F$, the integrals $\mathbb E_{\mu_C}[F X_{\Lambda,\epsilon}]$ converge with the bounds needed to normalize them; and (iii) as $\Lambda$ exhausts $\mathbb R^2$, the Schwinger hierarchy exists as tempered distributions, is Euclidean-invariant, permutation-symmetric, reflection-positive in the exact sense given by the earlier Euclidean-limit data, and has the required clustering and explicit per-order and uniform-order growth estimates. Any later reconstruction claim must name its precise theorem and prove that theorem's exact regularity and growth hypotheses; this contract does not identify the separately defined uniform-order bound with any reconstruction theorem's growth hypothesis. This contract asserts none of these interaction or infinite-volume conclusions. In particular, $L^2$ convergence of $U_{\Lambda,\epsilon}$ alone is not an exponential-integrability estimate.

items.title: L² convergence alone does not control exponential tilts

references.title: Stephen J. Summers, A Perspective on Constructive Quantum Field Theory, §3.1
references.locator: PDF pp. 10–12: the finite-volume P(φ)₂ measure requires exponential integrability; this item gives a separate elementary counterexample to inferring it from L² convergence.

references.title: Barry Simon, The P(φ)₂ Euclidean (Quantum) Field Theory, Chapter I, §1.1 (publisher preview)
references.locator: PDF pp. 24–33, printed pp. 4–13: the Gaussian/Wick setup motivating the distinction between an L² Wick limit and a normalized exponential tilt; the counterexample is proved locally.

items.statement: Under the Axiom of Choice and its countable-family consequence, on a probability space, if real random variables $U_n$ converge to $0$ in $L^2$, then their exponential normalizers $\mathbb E[e^{-U_n}]$ are uniformly bounded.
